title: How the Jerox site should feel
question: The desk clipboard leads. Keep it, take another way of showing the four jobs, or re-roll.

options.label: The Desk Clipboard
options.lineage: A hardboard clipboard on a dark desk blotter
options.thesis: What you just needed is still clipped to the board, and the rest of the desk is the app you were already in.
options.viewport: One clipboard on a dark green blotter. Four slips under the clip show the real panels. The empty blotter is the other app. No download button.
options.risk: Paper can turn into a stationery shop and bury the Mac interface the slips are meant to show.

raised.raise: The blotter stays mostly empty. That emptiness is the other app, and Jerox does not cover it.
The slips and the blotter are the only chrome. No stock cards, pills, or a software header.
Four slips in one sweep. Each slip owns one job: copy, rewrite, dictate, read the screen.

options.label: At the Cursor
options.lineage: The panel that opens on the caret
options.thesis: The page is the document you were writing, and Jerox appears at the cursor exactly as it does on the Mac.
options.viewport: A document fills the screen. The otter sits in the menu bar. The clipboard list opens at the caret, drawn like the app.
options.risk: This is the picture most clipboard apps already use: their own window floating on a document.

options.label: The Pattern Envelope
options.lineage: A home sewing pattern: envelope, tissue, and pins
options.thesis: The four jobs are pattern pieces. You pin them to the app you are already in, on grain, and you do not rotate off that work.
options.viewport: The envelope front lists views A to D. The tissue is the other app, with four pieces pinned along the fold.
options.case: The pieces make the four jobs and the return to your app obvious. A person mid-sentence does not see themselves at a sewing table.
options.risk: Dressmaking can smother a Mac tool if the tissue is costume instead of the instruction.

options.label: The Album Spread
options.lineage: A sticker album with numbered slots and ghost outlines
options.thesis: Four numbered slots. A filled slot is the real panel, sitting proud. An empty slot says which job is still missing.
materials: glossy stickers of the real UI
options.viewport: One album spread. Slots 1 to 4 are history, rewrite, dictate, and screen text, each sticker drawn from the app.
options.case: The slots make the four jobs scannable. Collecting stickers is not the moment someone is mid-sentence in another app.
options.risk: A half-filled album implies a set to complete, and Jerox is not a collection.

options.label: The Solidarity Sheet
options.lineage: A flat silkscreen poster with the message running around the edge
options.thesis: One emblem in the middle. The four jobs run around the edge as flat type. No pricing, no logo cloud, no software template.
options.viewport: A full-bleed sheet. The otter or the cursor panel is the emblem. Copy, rewrite, dictate, and read the screen ring the edge.
options.case: The offer is one picture and four true job names. A solidarity poster is not this person’s desk.
options.risk: The fist-and-slogan habit can shout over a tool whose whole point is staying quiet.

options.label: The Alcove
options.lineage: An ikebana arrangement in an empty plaster alcove
options.thesis: Almost nothing is on the page. One mark is Jerox. The empty field is the work you were doing.
options.viewport: A wide empty field with one off-center cluster naming the four jobs.
options.case: A person copying text does not read an alcove as a menu-bar app, and the offer disappears into the quiet.
options.kept: The empty field stays active. The other app is the page, and Jerox does not cover it.

options.label: The Night Board
options.lineage: A dial-up bulletin board in sixteen ANSI colors
options.thesis: The site is a text screen you dial into, with four numbered doors.
options.viewport: An 80-column title, then four numbered lines for the jobs.
options.case: Dialing into a board is the opposite of staying in the app you already have open.
options.kept: Slips and blotter are the only chrome. No stock cards.
options.risk: It leaves the Mac and becomes a terminal costume.

options.label: The Six-Pack
options.lineage: A small aircraft’s night instrument panel
options.thesis: Each round gauge owns one truth, and you read them in one sweep.
options.viewport: Four glowing dials for the four jobs, read left to right.
options.case: Paste-back and a cursor panel are not needle positions, and a cockpit is not this desk.
options.kept: Four slips, one sweep, each slip owns one job.
options.risk: The mechanism becomes a meter and the work disappears.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A centered headline, three feature cards, and a product shot. What app sites ship, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, three cards for the jobs, one product image, one quiet line of text. No price.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other app site by design.
